articles.title: Operação resgata DNA de araucária gigante que caiu em SC para clonagem | G1
articles.standfirst: Conhecida como Pinheirão, árvore tinha mais de 40 metros e permaneceu com brotos vivos meses após tombar. Pesquisadores já produziram cerca de 50 enxertos para tentar preservar seu patrimônio genético.
articles.summary: Conhecida como 'Pinheirão', árvore com mais de 40 metros tinha idade estimada entre 400 e 500 anos.
articles.body:
A queda de uma das maiores árvores do país mobilizou equipes de pesquisadores em uma verdadeira operação de resgate científico.

Conhecida carinhosamente como Pinheirão, a araucária de mais de 40 metros de altura ficava em uma floresta experimental compartilhada pela Embrapa Florestas e pela Empresa de Pesquisa Agropecuária e Extensão Rural de Santa Catarina (Epagri), no município de Caçador (SC).

A suspeita é de que a árvore tenha tombado em fevereiro deste ano, mas a queda só foi descoberta dois meses depois, no final de abril, durante a manutenção de uma estrada que corta a floresta.

Para garantir que a história e as características genéticas da árvore não se percam, cientistas da Embrapa foram ao local em busca de brotações vivas no tronco e nos galhos.

Pesquisador anda sob a araucária gigante que caiu em Santa Catarina. — Foto: Reprodução/Globo Rural

Durante o trabalho de campo, o especialista em clonagem Ivar Wendling, engenheiro florestal da Embrapa, surpreendeu-se ao encontrar ramos ainda emitindo brotos quatro meses após a queda. Além das amostras colhidas no chão, o pesquisador escalou uma araucária vizinha de grande porte para coletar brotos preservados na copa, a mais de 40 metros do solo.

O material recolhido foi levado para a sede da Embrapa Florestas, na Região Metropolitana de Curitiba.

Em estufa, os cientistas já produziram cerca de 50 clones a partir do método de enxertia. A técnica consiste em realizar uma pequena cirurgia vegetal, enxertando o ramo recolhido do Pinheirão em uma muda jovem produzida por semente.

Caso o enxerto se consolide após 100 dias, os pesquisadores obterão uma cópia com 100% do DNA da matriz gigante. O objetivo é conservar o patrimônio genético de uma árvore de longevidade e porte extraordinários.

Um disco de madeira do tronco do Pinheirão foi retirado e enviado ao laboratório no Paraná. — Foto: Reprodução Globo Rural

Além do resgate vegetativo, um disco de madeira do tronco do Pinheirão foi retirado e enviado ao laboratório no Paraná . Ele passará por um processo de secagem lenta para não rachar e, posteriormente, por polimento com lixas para evidenciar os anéis de crescimento.

Por meio da dendrocronologia — ciência que analisa as marcas anuais no tronco —, os cientistas conseguirão determinar a idade exata da árvore e reconstituir o histórico climático da região ao longo dos séculos. Estimativas iniciais indicam que a árvore tinha entre 400 e 500 anos quando tombou.

Em estudos semelhantes, o professor Marcelo Scipioni, do curso de engenharia florestal da Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina ( UFSC ), identificou 325 anéis em outra araucária gigante tombada que ocupava a 24ª posição no ranking nacional.

As análises revelam que anéis mais largos indicam anos mais quentes e chuvosos, enquanto marcas mais estreitas sinalizam períodos de seca.

O encharcamento do solo é o maior inimigo das araucárias centenárias. O excesso de água reduz a resistência das raízes e o peso da estrutura faz com que a árvore perca a sustentação e tombe. Com o passar dos séculos, o centro da madeira apodrece, formando cavidades internas que podem ultrapassar 10 metros de altura.

O trabalho de campo de Scipioni inclui o mapeamento das maiores araucárias que restaram no Brasil. Para a ciência, o gigantismo da espécie é definido a partir de 1,50 metro de diâmetro de tronco.

Atualmente, o mapa de distribuição das araucárias gigantes sobreviventes contabiliza poucas dezenas de exemplares:

A maior araucária do país fica na área rural de São Joaquim (SC), sendo a única registrada com mais de 3 metros de diâmetro e idade estimada em mais de 600 anos.

A escassez desses gigantes reflete a intensa devastação sofrida pela espécie. Durante o ciclo madeireiro, entre 1900 e 1970, a araucária foi a árvore mais derrubada do país.

Como consequência, hoje restam apenas 3% da cobertura florestal original, que no passado abrangia uma área de 200 mil quilômetros quadrados no Sul do Brasil (o equivalente ao dobro do território catarinense).

articles.title: Quem é o homem mais rico da África  | G1
articles.standfirst: Bilionário Aliko Dangote lançou a maior oferta pública inicial da história da África, ao listar sua refinaria de petróleo na bolsa de valores do país.
articles.summary: Bilionário Aliko Dangote lançou a maior oferta pública inicial da história da África, ao listar sua refinaria de petróleo na bolsa de valores do país.
articles.body:
Aliko Dangote afirma que os planos de expansão de sua empresa ajudarão os países africanos a se tornarem autossuficientes em energia. — Foto: Reprodução/Reuters

O homem mais rico da África, Aliko Dangote, lançou a maior oferta pública inicial de ações da história do continente. Ele está listando sua empresa de refinaria de petróleo, a Dangote, na bolsa de valores da Nigéria neste mês.

O bilionário nigeriano batizou a abertura de capital de "IPO [oferta pública inicial] do Povo" — promovendo a venda como uma oportunidade para os cidadãos possuírem parte de uma empresa que muitos nigerianos já consideram um patrimônio nacional.

A agência de notícias Reuters noticiou que, se todas as 4,1 bilhões de ações disponíveis forem vendidas, a empresa arrecadará 2,15 trilhões de nairas nigerianas — ou US$ 1,6 bilhão — para ajudar na expansão de sua refinaria, que já tem capacidade para processar cerca de 700 mil barris de petróleo bruto por dia.

No primeiro dia da venda de ações, os aplicativos de investimento tiveram dificuldades técnicas para lidar com a alta demanda pelas ações.

A Bamboo, empresa que administra uma das ferramentas de investimento mais populares da Nigéria, entrou em colapso após a venda de ações da Dangote — Foto: REUTERS

Apesar do grande entusiasmo de investidores, analistas alertam que os preços das ações podem cair ou subir.

"Eles deveriam investir apenas um dinheiro de que não precisarão pelos próximos três, quatro ou cinco anos", disse à BBC o consultor financeiro Abdulrazak Ibrahim Fagge.

Mas o que se sabe sobre Aliko Dangote, e sua promessa de trazer prosperidade e independência financeira a cidadãos africanos?

Aos 69 anos, Dangote é a pessoa mais rica da África, com uma fortuna superior a US$ 51,5 bilhões, segundo dados da revista Forbes de 20 de setembro.

Dangote domina os mercados de cimento, açúcar, sal e fertilizantes da Nigéria há décadas.

Em 2024, seu império representava um terço do valor de todas as empresas listadas na bolsa de valores nigeriana.

Ele é conhecido por seu temperamento ameno — e costuma dirigir seu próprio carro no trajeto entre reuniões.

Quando ainda estava na escola, ele comprava doces em grandes quantidades, contratava outras crianças para vendê-los e ficava com uma parte dos lucros.

O lado materno da sua família já possuia um grande patrimônio, e seu bisavô era o homem mais rico da África Ocidental quando morreu.

"Ele vem de uma família com tradição no mundo dos negócios", disse Lekan Sote, colunista do jornal nigeriano The Punch, à BBC.

Após se formar em administração de empresas, Dangote iniciou seu próprio negócio de comércio de commodities com um empréstimo de 500 mil nairas (então cerca de R$ 2 mil). Foi um grande sucesso e ele quitou o empréstimo em menos de 6 meses.

Hoje, seu portfólio inclui a Dangote Cement, a maior produtora de cimento da África, e a refinaria de petróleo Dangote, que iniciou a produção em 2024, e hoje é uma das maiores do mundo.

A estratégia de Dangote tem se concentrado na substituição de importações — o que significa que suas empresas produzem localmente bens que a Nigéria tradicionalmente compra do exterior.

Diversos países africanos sofrem com a incapacidade de processar suas matérias-primas e, consequentemente, comprar produtos processados a partir delas, o que aumenta os custos. Os governos frequentemente subsidiam os preços.

A possibilidade de criar um produto final localmente reduziria a necessidade desse tipo de suporte.

No entanto, os críticos da substituição de importações argumentam que os controles sobre a concorrência podem causar aumento de preços e impulsionar a inflação.

A Nigéria é o maior produtor de petróleo da África, mas até a inauguração da refinaria de Dangote, a maior parte do combustível do país era importada devido à falta de capacidade de refino. Isso significava que a Nigéria tinha que comprar petróleo refinado a um custo elevado.

Atualmente, a refinaria fornece mais de 70% do consumo de energia da Nigéria.

O documento sobre a oferta de ações afirma que a Dangote pretende dobrar a capacidade da refinaria.

Em 2024, a organização beneficente Oxfam relatou que Dangote "detém um 'quase monopólio' no setor de cimento na Nigéria. A expansão de seu império para o petróleo levantou preocupações sobre um novo monopólio privado."

Mas, segundo o jornalista Lekan Sote, alguns analistas acreditam que o bilionário está simplesmente preenchendo lacunas que o governo não consegue ocupar: "Ele sabe que o governo é lento. Qualquer pessoa que seja ousada o suficiente, que possa jogar pesado e estar presente nesse mercado, aproveitará o que está acontecendo."

Dangote nega acusações de praticar monopólios.

"Temos estado dispostos a investir de forma significativa, demonstrando o nosso compromisso com a excelência. Reconhecemos o potencial do setor manufatureiro na Nigéria e no resto da África, e o aproveitamos quando outros não conseguiram", disse.

Ele afirma que a expansão da refinaria impulsionará a independência econômica da região. No mês passado, ele disse à BBC que seus planos terão "um impacto enorme", ajudando algumas nações do continente a se tornarem autossuficientes em energia.

"Isso garante que os países recebam seu próprio produto. Eles não vão mais viver na miséria. A refinaria está lá, é para eles", disse ele.

Mas as afirmações de que a expansão da refinaria trará independência econômica a partes da África são "provavelmente exageradas", diz Sote. O jornalista, porém, reconhece que a refinaria poderá baixar preços na região "devido à economia de escala que surgirá quando a capacidade de produção eventualmente aumentar".

Os nigerianos podem ter economizado dinheiro com a redução dos preços de combustíveis, mas alguns argumentam que a riqueza gerada não está chegando às pessoas comuns.

Kingsley Moghalu, ex-vice-governador do Banco Central da Nigéria, escreveu no jornal nigeriano Premium Times em julho de 2025: "A riqueza de Dangote é pessoal. Ela não enriqueceu os nigerianos de forma significativa."

Mas ele questiona se enriquecer os nigerianos deveria ser uma preocupação de Dangote, que é, afinal, um homem de negócios.

As tentativas declaradas da empresa de aumentar a autossuficiência africana ajudaram a gerar entusiasmo em torno da venda de ações, disse à BBC o analista de investimentos Oluwasina Oluwaleke.

"A nação apoia firmemente essa iniciativa porque reconhece o impulso econômico para a independência, não apenas da Nigéria, mas da África Ocidental e da África em geral."

No entanto, Simon Jack, editor da BBC, afirma: "Há acusações de que Dangote não faz o suficiente pelas pessoas de baixa renda no norte da Nigéria e concentra sua riqueza no sul."

Os negócios de Dangote têm sido alvo de críticas devido aos seus impactos ambientais.

Em 2020, uma ação judicial foi movida contra o grupo Dangote em nome de pessoas que sofriam de problemas de saúde que estariam ligados à sua indústria de cimento.

A Dangote Cement pagou um pacote de indenização de US$ 270 mil para pessoas que moram nos arredores de uma de suas fábricas.

A demanda pelos produtos da refinaria foi impulsionada por interrupções no fornecimento relacionadas à guerra com o Irã — Foto: BBC via Getty

Dangote afirmou que deseja dar aos nigerianos comuns a oportunidade de participar do sucesso da refinaria de petróleo e "democratizar a criação de riqueza".

A compra mínima é de 5.525 nairas (equivalente a R$ 20) — um desembolso inferior ao de muitas outras ofertas de ações.

"Todos os dias, os nigerianos usam produtos que dependem de petróleo refinado. O que torna este IPO único é que ele oferece às pessoas a oportunidade não só de consumir, mas também de participar como proprietárias do sistema industrial que impulsiona a vida econômica", disse Dangote antes da venda.

Oluwaleke afirma que as interrupções no fornecimento relacionadas à guerra com o Irã aumentaram a demanda pelos produtos da refinaria, impulsionando a expectativa em torno da venda: "As redes sociais e os veículos de comunicação estão repletos de notícias."

No entanto, alguns analistas são mais cautelosos, acreditando que as ações se desvalorizarão se os altos lucros atuais desaparecerem.

Entre os investidores está Isah Salisu, que disse à BBC que retirou 50 mil nairas (R$ 190) de suas economias para investir.

"Minha esperança é que meu pequeno dinheiro um dia se multiplique. Não quero perder essa oportunidade, já que muitas pessoas que conheço também estão investindo", disse ele.

Mas o especialista em economia Abdulrazak Ibrahim Fagge alerta que o preço das ações pode vir a cair, o que significa que as pessoas poderiam perder parte do seu dinheiro.

Ele adverte: "O que os potenciais compradores, especialmente aqueles que estão comprando ações pela primeira vez, devem saber é que não devem investir todo o seu dinheiro — ou o dinheiro que precisarão em alguns meses."

articles.title: Trump’s DOJ probes major TV networks over response to White House ban of CNN
articles.summary: The Justice Department is investigating the five major US TV networks for possible antitrust violations, opening yet another front in the Trump administration’s pressure campaign against the press.
articles.body: The Justice Department is investigating the five major US TV networks for possible antitrust violations, opening yet another front in the Trump administration’s pressure campaign against the press. The probe, which one leading First Amendment group called nonsensical, concerns the TV pool, a long-standing arrangement that was disrupted last month when President Donald Trump banned CNN from the White House grounds. The pool is a small, rotating group of journalists that provides coverage of the president and represents the larger press corps. The TV pool chair at the time said that with Trump “preventing CNN from fulfilling its assigned pool duties,” there would be “no replacement pool put in place.” There was no pooled TV coverage of Trump’s events for several days until a federal judge issued an order temporarily halting Trump’s ban on CNN, MSNOW and Politico. That litigation is ongoing, and the Justice Department is defending Trump’s action in court. Now, the Justice Department is also probing how the TV pool functions. The highly unusual inquiry was first reported by The New York Times on Saturday. It comes two weeks after Trump ally Laura Loomer publicly encouraged the DOJ to challenge the networks on antitrust grounds. In a statement to CNN, a Justice Department spokesperson confirmed the contours of the investigation. “Members of the television press pool have boycotted covering White House events. Group boycotts among commercial competitors can violate the Sherman Act,” the spokesperson said. “The Antitrust Division is simply investigating to determine whether these news organizations have violated the antitrust laws.” Representatives for the five networks that have made up the pool for decades — ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC — either declined to comment or did not respond to requests for comment on Saturday night. Bruce D. Brown, president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, said the investigation “appears to be a pretext for seeking records from the networks about how they are covering daily White House events during a media ban the president himself put in place.” Brown added, “The decisions news organizations make about coverage are protected by the First Amendment, and summoning antitrust authority, on top of the retaliatory actions the White House has already taken to bar certain outlets, is another and even more brazen attempt to try to intimidate journalists.” Some of the networks first learned about the investigation on Friday, two sources with knowledge of the matter said, when attorneys for the networks received government demands for documents relating to the pool, including its formation and its recent operations. Through the pool, the five TV networks take turns documenting the president’s appearances, sharing live and taped footage with one another and the wider press corps. It’s a costly 365-day-a-year endeavor, with multi-day trips often costing tens of thousands of dollars for the networks involved. The TV pool system emerged out of necessity back in the era of the three broadcast networks. It enables a single TV crew to provide presidential event coverage for many news organizations when space or access is limited. Viewers worldwide are the beneficiaries. For example, presidential Q&As in the Oval Office and trips on Air Force One are typically covered by the pool. Local TV stations, newspaper websites and media outlets worldwide rely on the footage. Jonathan Kanter, the Biden administration’s assistant attorney general for antitrust, said any antitrust-violation claims will run into Supreme Court precedent that upheld civil rights-era boycotts as protected speech. “This is not even in the same zip code of an antitrust violation,” Kanter told CNN. “It’s literally freedom of speech.” The press pool coming together is a First Amendment-protected freedom, Kanter said. He noted that the press pool has existed for years, with cooperation from successive White Houses. Pool members cooperating in response to what they believe to be a First Amendment violation by the administration cannot suddenly become an antitrust issue. “It’s no more an antitrust violation than the reporters coming together to form the pool in the first place,” Kanter said. When Trump’s ban of CNN disrupted the pool operation, the five networks issued a rare joint statement that read, “The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.” The pool’s decision to stand with CNN — rather than put a replacement pool in place — was described in an email by Bryan Boughton, the Washington bureau chief for Fox News, who was the TV pool chair at the time. Chloe Arensberg, the DC bureau chief for NBC News, is now the TV pool chair. One of the sources with knowledge of the matter said the Justice Department probe may factor into the lawsuit CNN and the two other banned outlets, MS NOW and Politico, filed last month. Alleged retaliation against the news outlets has been a throughline in the legal filings by lawyers for CNN, MS NOW and Politico. The Freedom of the Press Foundation reacted to the news of the probe Saturday night by saying, “What nonsense.” “Trump may view the presidency as a business venture, but news outlets’ standing up for the First Amendment has nothing to do with antitrust law,” the advocacy group wrote on Bluesky. Nico Perrino, an executive vice president at the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression, invoked Trump’s inauguration day pledge to restore free speech and said the probe was another example of retribution. “Is there a lever this administration is unwilling to pull to punish its enemies?” Perrino wrote on X. “So much for ‘bringing free speech back to America’ and ending the lawfare.”

articles.title: India targets 604 million tons of steel capacity by 2047, eyes lower emissions
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India has set an ambitious target to nearly triple its steelmaking capacity to 604 million metric tons by 2047 from around 220 million tons at
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India has set an ambitious target to nearly triple its steelmaking capacity to 604 million metric tons by 2047 from around 220 million tons at present, while planning to reduce carbon emissions and secure long-term supplies of key raw materials, according to a draft steel policy released for public consultation.Reuters reported last week, citing the draft document, that the proposed policy outlines measures to cut emissions from steel production and strengthen access to iron ore and coking coal as India prepares for rising demand. The draft was released for public consultation late on Saturday.Under the proposed policy, India aims to reduce the steel sector's average carbon-emission intensity to around 1.54 tons of carbon dioxide per ton of crude steel by 2047, down from the current 2.54 tons.The reduction of nearly 39 per cent is intended to support India's broader commitment to achieving net-zero emissions by 2070.Meeting the capacity target will also require a substantial increase in raw-material supplies. The steel ministry projects iron ore demand at 772 million tons and plans to secure access to high-grade reserves through overseas investments and joint ventures, according to the draft.Coking coal demand is expected to reach 236 million tons, the document said. To reduce supply risks, the government plans to diversify sourcing through what it describes as "strategic global outreach" and the acquisition of overseas assets.The proposed expansion comes as India seeks to strengthen its industrial base and meet the steel requirements of infrastructure development, construction and manufacturing.However, increasing capacity while lowering emissions presents a significant challenge for an industry that relies heavily on coal-based production.The policy's success will depend on investment in new steelmaking facilities, access to reliable raw materials and the adoption of cleaner production technologies. articles.title: WWE Universe Reacts to Je’Von Evans’ 20-Foot Freefall Through Ambulance
articles.summary: Carnage was in ample supply during the Men’s Money in the Bank Ladder match on Saturday in New Orleans.Bron Breakker simultaneously speared CM Punk and Kevin...
articles.body:
Carnage was in ample supply during the Men's Money in the Bank Ladder match on Saturday in New Orleans.

Bron Breakker simultaneously speared CM Punk and Kevin Owens through the ringside barricade, Penta executed a Mexican Destroyer on a ladder, and Lil Yachty was hit with a stunner following an unsuccessful climb up the ladder.

In pursuit of the prized Money in the Bank briefcase, every participant risked life and limb in the main event match.

Perhaps nobody suffered a higher physical toll than Je'Von Evans, though.

Evans, the youngest Money in the Bank participant in WWE history, was stretchered backstage and loaded onto an ambulance truck after being struck with a devastating Spear from Bron Breakker.

Roughly ten minutes later, the 22-year-old high-flyer made a shocking return, driving the ambulance down the ramp and parking it at ringside.

Despite his severely damaged ribs, Evans put on a gutsy performance in the second half of the match.

He briefly wiped out Trick Williams and Penta before climbing up for the briefcase.

Reaching the ladder's summit ultimately led to his downfall, as Breakker tipped it over, launching Evans through the roof of the ringside ambulance truck.

WWE Universe Reacts to Insane Ambulance Spot

WWE fans have seen some crazy things through the years. Jeff Hardy jumped off a billboard, Undertaker tossed Mankind off the Hell in a Cell and through a table, and Edge once speared a man through a flaming table.

Although it likely came at the expense of a few broken ribs, Je'Von Evans delivered another unforgettable moment at Money in the Bank .

His crash landing through the ambulance has sent the internet into a frenzy , leaving the WWE Universe stunned .

"Well, at least paramedics don't have to waste time getting him wheeled in the ambulance and taken to the hospital. He has been fast-tracked inside," one fan joked.

"As soon as I saw that massive ladder I knew they were about to pull some bat sh*t crazy stunt," another commented.

One Instagram user wrote: "As Jim Ross would famously say in 1998: ' AS GOD AS MAY WITNESS, HE IS BROKEN IN HALF !'"

"Je'Von Evans died for our entertainment," a fan joked.

"This man just died," a fan said of Evans.

"Bro Je'Von about to wake up in the morning and not be able to move," someone commented.

" ONE OF THE MOST INSANE SPOTS IN WWE HISTORY ," an Instagram user commented.

Bron Breakker dominated the field for the majority of the contest, but Penta ultimately prevailed in the Men's Money in the Bank Ladder match.

The former Intercontinental Champion is now in prime position to secure his first World Championship.

He could pursue a rematch with World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns after their five-star bout in Mexico City.

Or, he could challenge current WWE Undisputed Champion Sami Zayn.

Either way, it will be interesting to see the fearless luchador competing for a world title.

articles.title: Precio de la luz por horas hoy, domingo 11 de octubre: cuándo es más barata y más cara en el día
articles.standfirst: El precio de la luz se encarece un 8.84 en domingo
articles.summary: El precio de la luz se encarece un 8.84 en domingo
articles.body: En este domingo, el precio medio de la electricidad se sitúa en 141,49 €/MWh, lo que supone un aumento de 11,49 € respecto al día anterior, cuando alcanzó los 130 €/MWh. Este incremento puede afectar a los usuarios que buscan reducir sus costes. A continuación, se analizarán las horas más caras y más baratas para aprovechar al máximo la tarifa eléctrica. Los precios de la luz alcanzan su punto más alto en las franjas horarias nocturnas y vespertinas, donde se concentran las tarifas más elevadas. A lo largo de la jornada, se destacan las horas comprendidas entre las 19:00 - 20:00 y 21:00 - 22:00, con valores que superan los 230 €/MWh, alcanzando un máximo de 234.79 €/MWh a las 19:00. Además, se observa un notable aumento en la franja de 18:00 - 19:00 con 178.46 €/MWh y un aumento continuo que se mantiene hasta la 22:00 - 23:00. La luz es más barata en las primeras horas de la mañana y en la tarde, con oportunidades significativas entre la 1:00 y las 16:00. En particular, las franjas horarias más relevantes para el ahorro energético son 12:00 - 13:00 y 15:00 - 16:00, donde los precios alcanzan niveles extremadamente bajos, de 1.2 €/MWh y 0.52 €/MWh, respectivamente. Además, existe una ventana amplia de precios bajos desde la 10:00 hasta las 16:00, donde los costos se mantienen en cifras que permiten un ahorro considerable. En el análisis de la jornada se destaca una **notable diferencia** entre el precio más barato y el más caro de la electricidad, que alcanza los **234,27 €/MWh**. Esta amplitud de precios refleja una *volatilidad significativa* a lo largo del día, lo que es crucial para los consumidores que buscan optimizar su consumo y minimizar costos. articles.title: Argentina pierde más de 32.000 empresas y 437.000 empleos formales en los primeros meses de la gestión de Milei
articles.standfirst: Así lo dice un informe del Centro de Economía Política Argentina (CEPA) y datos de la Superintendencia de Riesgos del Trabajo (SRT)
articles.summary: Así lo dice un informe del Centro de Economía Política Argentina (CEPA) y datos de la Superintendencia de Riesgos del Trabajo (SRT)
articles.body: Un informe del Centro de Economía Política Argentina (CEPA) y datos de la Superintendencia de Riesgos del Trabajo (SRT) confirman que, entre diciembre de 2023 y julio pasado, la economía argentina experimentó una notable reducción de su tejido productivo, registrando la pérdida de 32.290 empresas empleadoras (una contracción del 6,3%) y la destrucción de 437.611 puestos de trabajo formales. El cierre de empresas ha promediado una velocidad de 30 a 33 establecimientos diarios. Si bien, el universo afectado se concentra en pequeñas y medianas empresas (pymes), el volumen de pérdida de puestos de trabajo se acentúa en las corporaciones de mayor escala. El 99,63% de las firmas contaban con menos de 500 empleados y cerca de 188.525 (68,15%) empleos perdidos pertenecían a grandes compañías. Según diversos análisis, entre las causas que ha podido provocar esta situación aparecen una caída del consumo interno (las ventas sufrieron un retroceso del 10% debido a la pérdida del poder adquisitivo), aumento de costes de servicio (las tarifas de servicios públicos básicos se encarecieron un 249%) o la apreciación del peso (esto encarece los precios). La recesión golpeó con especial fuerza a las actividades ligadas a la infraestructura estatal y al mercado doméstico (como la construcción y administración pública), mientras que los campos primarios y extractivos mostraron una tendencia opuesta (destacan la minería, hidrocarburos y energía). A pesar de ello, el Gobierno argentino matiza estas cifras señalando que la baja en los registros patronales de la SRT no se traduce linealmente en quiebras definitivas, adjudicando parte de los movimientos a reorganizaciones societarias, fusiones o modificaciones en las nóminas laborales. Desde la perspectiva oficialista se prioriza el ordenamiento macroeconómico, destacando la consecución del superávit fiscal y los indicios de estabilización técnica del Producto Interno Bruto.

articles.title: Musk vows ‘affordable’ Starlink in India as he escalates feud with Ambani
articles.summary: Pledge comes days before Mukesh Ambani’s low-cost Reliance Jio’s parent launches India’s largest-ever IPO.
articles.body:
‌Billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk has said he would price his Starlink satellite internet service affordably ⁠in India to take ⁠on Mukesh Ambani’s low-cost Reliance Jio, escalating his attacks on the rival tycoon days before Jio’s parent launches the country’s largest-ever initial public offering (IPO).

Jio Platforms, ⁠which owns the telecom arm, is targeting a valuation of $106bn in the offering. Much like SpaceX-owned Starlink, Jio’s satellite venture is also awaiting final ⁠security clearance to launch.

Cheap data is the playbook that built Jio in India, and the one Musk has used in markets like Kenya to unsettle local telecom players. SpaceX now plans to enter the mobile carrier market itself, starting in ‌the United States.

Musk did not specify prices for India, where mobile data costs about rupees 7.74 ($0.08) per gigabyte, among the lowest in the world.

“Obviously, if Starlink is too expensive in India, no one will buy it, so SpaceX will need to make pricing affordable,” he said in a post on his social media platform X on Saturday.

“The reality is that ⁠competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by ⁠giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani’s profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business,” Musk added.

Musk’s remarks were the latest in ⁠a series of X posts in which he accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government and Ambani of stalling Starlink’s entry ⁠into one of the world’s biggest internet markets to ⁠favour market leader Jio.

The posts have marked a sharp turn for Musk, who has long enjoyed a warm public rapport with Modi.

India’s government has denied any bias in its approval process, ‌noting that the three satellite ventures seeking to launch, including Starlink’s and Jio’s, are all awaiting final security clearance.

Late on Friday, Musk taunted Ambani directly, addressing ‌him as “Prime ‌Minister Ambani” and asking whether he would “consider allowing Starlink to compete”.

Reliance has not responded to Musk’s remarks.

articles.title: AM radio is disappearing from cars. Congress wants to stop that
articles.summary: Chances are the last time you listened to a traditional radio was in a car.
articles.body: Chances are the last time you listened to a traditional radio was in a car. Maybe you tuned in to a ballgame, a local news report, or a weather or traffic update. Maybe there’s even a talk or music station you’ve listened to for years, if not decades. In a car, it can be as simple as just tapping a button — much easier than finding it on your phone. Broadcasters are fighting to make sure that doesn’t have to change. Legislation passed in the House last month that would require all new cars to have an AM radio. Backers of the bill say the century-old tech is critical to ensuring all Americans still have a way to access emergency information. Radios have been standard equipment in cars since before most of today’s drivers were born. The overwhelming majority of vehicles do include them. But automakers like Tesla, Volkswagen and Volvo have been removing AM radios from some newer models over the past few years, especially electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids, since EV motors affect the sound. “EVs and AM broadcasting technologies don’t always mix,” said John Bozzella, CEO of industry trade group Alliance for Automotive Innovation, during congressional testimony in April 2024. “The high-voltage electrical systems in EVs generate electromagnetic interference…. distort AM radio signals, affecting the listening experience for drivers and passengers. In other words: really staticky.” Auto industry research finds that drivers rarely listen to analog AM radio, instead tuning in to streaming and satellite radio or digital AM and FM broadcasts. But the National Association of Broadcasters, who represent the radio stations, argues there are serious safety reasons to keep analog AM radio in cars. Fewer and fewer American households have a traditional radio in their home, which can be an important source for emergency warnings during events like hurricanes, wildfires or terrorist attacks. That’s because some emergency situations can disrupt cell service, or a rush of usage can overwhelm networks, blocking phone alerts. “When the power goes out, radio can often be that sole lifeline, and AM radio in particular has a reach and a durability that that other media just don’t simply have,” said Curtis LeGeyt, CEO of NAB. Car radios are also critical to keeping radio stations in business. Fifty-three percent of the audience for AM and FM radio listen in cars, according to the NAB. That’s a big audience to lose. AM radio is still used by more than 4,000 stations across the country, according to the Federal Communications Commission. That includes sports and talk radio, as well as religious programming and foreign language news, sports and music. The NAB says 82 million Americans listen to AM radio every month, and that broadcasts are particularly vital for rural and tribal communities where internet and cellular connection can be unreliable. But automakers are always looking for ways to cut costs, said Ivan Drury, director of insights at car buying site Edmunds. If companies can save a little money by eliminating something they believe their customers don’t care about, they will. “It might be that the cost of a single unit is downright silly,” said Drury, noting that an AM radio adds less than one-tenth of 1% to the cost of building the typical new car. “But when you make millions of them, it becomes significant.” The automakers also object to the government interfering in parts of the design that don’t improve the safety of the vehicle, saying a radio is different from seat belts and air bags. “Congress is opening a space for (the National Highway Safety Administration) to mandate vehicle equipment that falls outside the vehicle safety lane,” Bozzella testified. “NHTSA should be a vehicle safety agency – and an agency with boundaries.” But the legislation, which heads to the Senate, does have significant bipartisan support. While it won’t get a vote before the midterm election next month, its supporters hope it passes in the lame duck session between election day and when the new Congress is seated. “If it was put up for a vote tomorrow, it would pass overwhelmingly,” said LeGeyt.

articles.title: Gonzalo Bernardos, economista, sobre el dilema de Rufián: “Si uno ha venido a la política a servir escoge la segunda opción, si ha venido a vivir de ella elige la primera”
articles.standfirst: El experto financiero se ha pronunciado en su cuenta de X
articles.summary: El experto financiero se ha pronunciado en su cuenta de X
articles.body: Gabriel Rufián ya dejó claro hace unos días que su deseo es representar a Esquerra Republicana (ERC) en el Congreso de los Diputados. Sin embargo, eso no implica que quiera hacerlo bajo "unas mínimas condiciones", tal y como señaló mediante un mensaje en su cuenta de X. Dicho esto, el portavoz catalán continúa en un periodo de reflexión y a la espera de que el partido responda a estas exigencias. Como era de esperar, este escenario en torno al futuro de Rfuián ha generado muchas opiniones en nuestro país. Entre ellas, ha destacado la del economista Gonzalo Bernardos, quien también ha utilizado la mencionada red social para dar su punto de vista sobre el comportamiento del diputado. “Rufián no se ha atrevido a dar el salto sin red a Frente Amplio y Junqueras no se ha atrevido a depurarlo, a pesar de que muchos de sus colaboradores se lo pedían. En el próximo Congreso, tendremos dos Rufián: él y Ada Colau, que competirán por ver quién la dice más gorda”, señalaba el también profesor en la Universidad de Barcelona, antes de pasar al posible dilema que podría tener el político. Aunque el economista presenta que la gran duda de Rufián está entre elegir “cuatro años más siendo un verso libre en ERC” o “arriesgarme e intentar unir la extrema izquierda española”, él tiene claro cuál es su elección. “Si uno ha venido a la política a servir escoge la segunda opción, si ha venido a vivir de ella elige la primera. Ya sabéis que ha elegido Rufián”, sentencia Bernardos tajante. Cabe destacar que, ante la incertidumbre sobre la decisión final de Rufián, la dirección de Esquerra Republicana ya tiene una clara alternativa. Se trata de Jordi Albert, persona de confianza de Oriol Junqueras, y actual portavoz de la formación en el Parlamento de Cataluña.

articles.title: To counteract a spooky economy, America prepares to spend on Halloween candy
articles.summary: This Halloween, rising prices for groceries and gas are pushing many consumers to cut back. But they’re not giving up Halloween candy.
articles.body: This Halloween, the fright isn’t just at the haunted house. Rising prices for everything from groceries to gas are driving many consumers to cut back. “I’m walking to save a little bit of money,” said Lakisha Reardon, a legal assistant. “I’m bringing in my own lunch.” Reardon said she has especially seen her electric bill spike this year. She said she is paying an extra $150 every month. “I’m ready to invest in candles,” she said. But one thing she won’t give up? Halloween candy. Average prices for chewing gum and candy have soared 8.1% over the last year, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Despite the higher prices, Americans are still buying treats. “I remember being a little kid and being super excited when I would get Reese’s Cups,” said Abby Mynatt, a college student who lives in Knoxville, Tennessee. “I want to give that to some other children.” Mynatt, 21, said she usually spends around $50 for Halloween candy. She is expecting to shell out a bit more money this year despite financial pressures. “I certainly think there are a little more tense things with my budget right now,” she said. “But I still think that certain things, even just little pleasures, are still worth it.” The price of nonchocolate candy items has averaged $3.31 this year, up 1.8% from last year, according to PwC. But Halloween chocolate prices have jumped 15.5%, to an average of $5.67 per package. Industry experts attribute the rise in chocolate prices partly to a cocoa shock over the last couple years. Extreme weather in key cocoa-producing countries like Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana sent global cocoa prices soaring — they quadrupled from January 2023 to January 2025, according to data from the International Monetary Fund. “Because chocolate makers buy cocoa months, sometimes up to two years ahead, shoppers are paying for that spike now,” said Ali Furman, PwC’s consumer markets industry leader. “Cocoa prices have since fallen by about half, but lower costs take time to reach the shelf and won’t show up on shelves this Halloween season.” The market research firm NIQ has seen a more muted increase in prices, with chocolate overall up 9.4% from a year ago but Halloween-specific chocolate just up 1.7%. Analysts say tariffs this year aren’t helping, either. In July, the U.S. imposed tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on 60 trade partners. “Chocolate comes from elsewhere, so tariffs being added onto it have certainly increased costs that manufacturers are feeling as well,” said Chris Costagli, the leader of food and nonalcoholic beverage insights at NIQ. Still, the National Retail Federation projects that Halloween spending will soar to $13.5 billion this season, with 96% of Halloween shoppers expecting to buy sweets. It’s part of a broader trend this year of consumers leaning into little luxuries like makeup and movie tickets as an antidote for economic gloom. A lot of that gloom stems from concerns about inflation and the rising cost of living. Consumer prices have jumped 3.4% over the last year in large part due to rising energy costs, according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. With wages up just 3% over the same period, paychecks aren’t keeping up with prices. It has led many people to forgo bigger purchases and cut back in small ways every day. Leonard Smith is planning to buy Halloween candy this year, but says he may cut back. “I don’t want to spend that much money because I need money for other things besides candy,” said Smith, 36, who lives in Delaware. But he has a strategy to save: Smith buys candy after Halloween when many stores slash prices. Ari Monahan, a nanny who describes herself as “like a Disney adult, but for Halloween,” said she may get candy that’s a little less expensive, but she still wants to treat the kids in her New York City neighborhood. “I want to be the good house,” she said. “There’s not that many kids in my area, so I want to give them a little prize for coming.” Monahan, 30, also buys little treats for herself. “Dark chocolate, a lot of coffees, anything pumpkin spice,” she said. “If it makes me smile and I have a little money, I’ll pay for it because everything is so grim right now,” she added. “A pair of socks with dachshunds on it, I’m like, ‘You know what? I can do that. I could swing it today.’” Monahan says rising prices are taking a big bite out of her paycheck, and she worries she might never be able to buy a house. Home prices are near record highs, and mortgage rates have spiked over the course of the war with Iran — with the 30-year fixed rate topping 7.6% earlier this month, a nearly three-year high. It’s a double whammy that is putting a key pillar of the American dream further out of reach for many people. And yet in an economy where the big things might seem far away, there are always little treats to get by. “I’ve been in a real ‘buy yourself little treats’ mentality,” said Monahan. “I keep buying too much stuff for my dog. I guess I didn’t buy another dog. That’s saving, right?”

articles.title: Bond yields are surging worldwide — and France is on the 'ugly side': Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Sharp rises in bond yields are happening worldwide, but for different reasons, say strategists.
articles.body:
It's not just the US seeing a rapid rise in bond yields . The surge in Treasury yields worldwide is raising alarm bells among investors.

"Any lingering doubts about whether the world has truly left the era of low interest rates behind should now be quashed," Thomas Garretson, senior portfolio strategist at RBC Wealth Management, wrote in a recent note.

Longer-dated bond yields have been flagging issues "that have been percolating in global bond markets for years, which are now coming to a head," he noted.

Wall Street strategists see an array of reasons behind the rise in yields.

"On the good side of the spectrum, better-than-expected economic growth has driven US bond yields up to levels that are back to normal," Ed Yardeni of Yardeni Research wrote last week.

"On the ugly side, soaring bond yields in France are signaling a looming debt crisis ," he said.

The protests over public education funding across major French cities have coincided with surging bond yields.

Macquarie strategists have argued that there is a "direct and self-reinforcing causal connection" between recent street riots over proposed budget cuts in France and the country's bond market stress.

Behind France, the US 10-year yield ( ^TNX ) has posted its biggest jump among more than 20 countries tracked by Yardeni Research.

Italy, Indonesia, Japan, and South Korea have also seen their benchmark yields rise at least 100 basis points since the start of the year.

Rising yields are also attributed to higher oil prices stemming from the war in the Middle East and the unwinding of the yen-carry trade.

Japanese investors, who accumulated over $1.3 trillion in US Treasurys during the era of negative domestic rates, have been repatriating capital as domestic yields normalize.

RBC research estimates that every $100 billion shift in Japanese holdings impacts 10-year Treasury yields by roughly 50 basis points. As of July 2026, Japan's holdings are down $120 billion so far this year and about $300 billion from their 2021 peak.

As the US 10-year Treasury yield hangs near its highest level in 24 years, strategists are seeing a risk of 6% for the first time since 2000.

Even as bond yields revert to their levels prior to the 2008 financial crisis, strong earnings reports, coupled with a pause in interest rate hikes from the Fed , are expected to keep the stock market rally intact headed into the end of the year.

Seasonal tailwinds during midterm election years also favor a positive return for the S&P 500 this quarter.

Ines Ferre is a Senior Business Reporter for Yahoo Finance covering the US stock market, publicly traded companies, and commodities.
